heroHeadline: 21 Days to Kickoff — Iran Applies for US Visas in Ankara After Zurich Summit; Germany's Neuer Returns From Retirement
heroSubtitle: Iran's World Cup visa crisis moved to a breakthrough phase on May 21: squad players physically traveled to the US Embassy in Ankara, Turkey to submit visa applications — the first concrete step toward tournament travel — taken the day after the decisive FIFA-Infantino-Taj Zurich summit (May 20). FIFA President Infantino and Iran Football Federation chief Mehdi Taj met in Zurich on May 20; Taj confirmed FIFA 'listened to Iran's arguments, the ten points we raised, and offered solutions for each one.' FIFA reaffirmed Iran's participation in all three Group G matches on US soil (SoFi Stadium, Los Angeles: June 15 vs New Zealand, June 21 vs Belgium; Lumen Field, Seattle: June 26 vs Egypt). No US visas have yet been formally approved. The June 1 squad submission deadline is 11 days away. Iran's warm-up friendly vs The Gambia in Antalya is May 29. Germany head coach Julian Nagelsmann announced his 26-man squad on May 21 with the defining headline: Manuel Neuer (40, Bayern Munich) returning from international retirement as first-choice goalkeeper — making him Germany's oldest-ever World Cup squad member. Kimmich captains; Jamal Musiala, Florian Wirtz lead the attack; Antonio Rüdiger, Jonathan Tah, Waldemar Anton, Malick Thiaw in defence. Notable omissions: Serge Gnabry (injury), Niclas Füllkrug, Karim Adeyemi. Germany in Group E: Curaçao (June 14, NRG Stadium Houston), Ivory Coast (June 20, BMO Field Toronto), Ecuador (June 25, MetLife Stadium NJ). The squad wave continues: England (Tuchel at Wembley, May 22 — Ben White out MCL), Spain (De La Fuente, May 25 — Lamine Yamal and Fermín López both facing fitness concerns), USMNT (Pochettino, live NYC event on FOX, May 26 — Pulisic, McKennie, Adams, Balogun expected). Norway confirmed Erling Haaland in their squad (Solbakken, May 21), Senegal confirmed Sadio Mané (Cissé, May 21) — both meet in Group I alongside France and Iraq. Egypt confirmed Mohamed Salah (May 20) despite his late-season Liverpool hamstring injury. Final rosters due June 1; FIFA publishes all 48 squads simultaneously June 2.
